page: OVHcloud b3-640 is a general-purpose instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 160 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores running at 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core, paired with 640 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is equipped with a 20 Gbps baseline network interface.

In benchmark evaluations, the b3-640 demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem is highly efficient, achieving top-tier results in small-block read-only memory bandwidth and strong performance in large-block read/write operations. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware support for AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA.

This instance is highly suited for highly parallelized workloads, including software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput Redis deployments, where it achieves top-tier transaction rates. While prompt processing for large language models performs strongly, text generation for large 70B models is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The dedicated physical core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization jitter, making it a cost-efficient choice for high-density enterprise applications.
description: OVHcloud b3-640 is a high-density general-purpose instance featuring 160 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores at 2.3 GHz and 640 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it includes a 400 GB NVMe SSD and a 20 Gbps network interface. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, excelling in parallel processing tasks such as software compilation, database operations, and Redis caching. While it offers exceptional throughput for multi-threaded workloads, the lack of hardware GPU acceleration limits its efficiency for large-scale LLM text generation. It represents a highly capable option for resource-intensive enterprise applications requiring dedicated compute resources.
